decisions: 1. Same-state fakes: the state word stays; suburb and postcode come from a real locality of that state (a fake_pool=1 row of suburb list v2). A setting can switch to other states.

2. A suburb + state + postcode written together without a street line is an address, except right after a label or phrase that names another kind of place (birth, injury, accident or incident, declaration): those stay, postcode included. A place written with a postcode after a court's or hospital's name is replaced, and the name stays outside the unit.

3. A street named in running text without a house number is kept, and so is a street with a suburb but no house number, state or postcode ('injured on Victoria Road, Ryde'): both words stay. The same street followed by its suburb, state and postcode is an address. Only a place that directly follows the street (an optional comma, then the place) is its locality: a place named later, after other words, follows decision 2 on its own.
4. Tool 1's frozen baselines get fixed new versions labelled post-exposure: no effect on the expected results here.

5. All tool 2 profiles replace whole addresses as one unit: units, roles, structure words, look-alikes and same-fake groups hold in every profile. kept_places hold in the client profile; other profiles follow their own rule for places on their own.
6. Joel's tool gets no changes and is graded on its own redacted text: its prototype cases are inputs only.
7. The ABS suburb and postcode list (suburb list v2, with its alias and cross-border files) is the gazetteer and the fake pool for tools 1 and 2.

Overseas addresses (settled later on 2026-10-22): replaced whole as one unit; the country word stays, like 'Australia'; the fake keeps the shape (every number, the street name and type, the town and every postcode character change, digit for digit and letter for letter), with no foreign gazetteer.

Unchanged: a suburb, town, state or postcode on its own is kept; role words such as 'the claimant' stay; every address of anyone is replaced, persons' and organisations' alike; legislation and guideline citations are never addresses.
positions: [line, word]: the line's index in the case's 'lines' and the word's index in that line's text split on whitespace (punctuation stays attached to its word). Both count from 0.

building.rule: Building or property name words, the building word included ('Westpoint Tower', 'Kilbride Station', 'Riverside House'): pool words; the building word changes too.

designator.rule: Australia Post's unit and floor words and their abbreviations: Unit (U), Apartment (Apt), Flat (F), Factory (FY), House (HSE), Office (OFF), Penthouse (PTHS), Room (RM), Shop, Studio (STU), Suite (SE, Ste), Townhouse (TNHS), Villa, Warehouse (WE), Lot; Level (L, Lvl), Floor (FL), Ground Floor (G), Lower Ground Floor (LG), Upper Ground Floor (UG), Mezzanine (M), Basement (B); and 'Building', 'Block', 'Tower' and 'Wing' before a letter or number designator ('Building C', 'Tower 2'). Ground, Lower Ground, Upper Ground, Mezzanine and Basement need no number. Stays as written.

unit_number.rule: The number or letter after a unit, building, block, tower or wing word: the number rule; a letter becomes another letter.

level_number.rule: The number after 'Level', 'Floor' or 'Fl', or before 'Floor' (an ordinal keeps its suffix): another realistic level, 1-25 (1-5 when the fake suburb is regional), with no digit equal to the original's at its position.

number.rule: House number, ranges and letter suffixes included: the number rule.

unit_number+number.rule: A '5/3' unit/number word: both numbers follow the number rule; the slash stays. A level-type code before the unit number ('B02/53') stays, like a designator.

street_name.rule: Street-name words: a pool name in the original's case.

street_type.rule: Street type: another canonical type in the original's style (abbreviated stays abbreviated, plural stays plural, case kept). AS 4590 and AS/NZS 4819 abbreviations map to one canonical type ('Cres' and 'Cr' are both Crescent).

street_suffix.rule: A street-type suffix after the type ('Smith Street North'): another directional in the original's style (N, Nth or North).

corner.rule: 'Cnr', '&', and their spelled-out forms 'Corner', 'of', 'and' inside a corner form: stay.

box_kind.rule: Australia Post's postal delivery types: PO Box, P.O. Box, Post Office Box, GPO Box, Locked Bag, Locked Mail Bag, Private Bag, Private Mail Bag, Reply Paid, RMB (R.M.B.), RSD, CMB, PMB, MS, RMS, CMA, CPA, Care PO. Care PO, CMA, CPA and CMB may stand without a number. They stay; 'GPO' becomes 'PO' unless the fake suburb is a capital city, and stays 'GPO' when there is no fake suburb (no locality, or 'IN YOUR CAPITAL CITY').

box_number.rule: Box or bag number: the number rule.

box_extra.rule: Words between the box number and the place that are not a road ('City East'): replaced (fail closed). A road after the box number ('RMB 4600 Lakes Road') takes the street_name and street_type roles.

via.rule: 'via' between a property name and its place ('Kilbride Station via Berrima'): stays.

dx_exchange.rule: DX exchange: a fake locality of the same state, in the original's case.

suburb.rule: A real locality of the same state and class (metro or regional), drawn from the fake_pool=1 rows of suburb list v2, that shares no word with the original, in the original's case. In an overseas unit it is the town: it changes to a pool name in the original's case, with no foreign gazetteer.

state.rule: Stays exactly as written (same-state fakes, owner decision 1).

postcode.rule: The fake suburb's own postcode: never the original. The original's leading digits that match its state's prefix ('2' NSW and ACT, '3' VIC, '4' QLD, '5' SA, '6' WA, '7' TAS, '08' NT), matched from the left, may stay; every later digit differs at its position. OCR letters in the original ('275O') count as digits; the fake is written in digits. In an overseas unit every character changes, digit for digit and letter for letter, in the original's case and shape (a space between two postcode words stays).

state+postcode.rule: A state glued to its postcode ('NSW2750'): the state letters stay, the digits follow the postcode rule, and the fake stays glued.

country.rule: 'Australia', or the country that ends an overseas address ('New Zealand', 'UNITED KINGDOM'): stays.

capital_city_phrase.rule: 'IN YOUR CAPITAL CITY', written in place of a locality (Australia Post's form for national agencies): names no place and stays as written.

fake_constraints: A case's identifying words are the words of its units whose role is not a structure role; for a word with partial_structure, only its changing part.

No fake word or number may equal an identifying word or number of any address unit in the same case, in any role, after normalising both: case folded, curly apostrophes made straight, dots, apostrophes and hyphens removed, and 'Mt' and 'Mount', 'St' and 'Saint', 'Pt' and 'Point' read as one word. Numbers compare as whole digit runs.
A fake word must not begin with or contain an identifying word of 3 or more letters, and must not be one edit from one of 5 or more letters.

So the fake locality is drawn after filtering the pool by every identifying word of the case (street name and type, building, box extra, DX exchange, the other units' words), and the street-name and street-type pools are filtered by its suburb words.
Level numbers follow the positional digit rule: no digit equal to the original's at its position.
A number range with no fake that keeps both digit counts ('8-10', '98-104') lets each end keep its own digit count; every digit still differs at its position, and the range stays ascending.

An overseas unit (marked 'overseas': it ends in a country other than Australia) is replaced whole, keeping its shape, with no state and no gazetteer (the owner's ruling on overseas addresses): every number, the street name and type, the town and every postcode character change, digit for digit and letter for letter; the country word stays. No Australian state is ever inferred from its postcode.

title_and_name.note: the title is an optional word

gazetteer.detection: A place counts when its suburb is a name of its state (a v2 row of either source, or an alias) and its postcode lies in the state's Australia Post ranges or is a listed cross-border pair. Detection never requires the exact suburb-postcode pair, so PO-box postcodes (Darlinghurst NSW 1300) count.
gazetteer.fakes: Fake suburbs and postcodes come only from rows with fake_pool=1 (primary, in the state's range, population 200 or more, not a non-address area). Cross-border rows are real places but never fakes.

tiers.core: The owner's decisions and the plan's precision rules decide it, and the plan's join (with its amendments, PLAN_AMENDMENTS.md) is designed to reach it. A tool should pass it when its address work ships.
tiers.stretch: The expected result follows from the owner's decisions, but the plan's rules are known not to reach it yet (noted per case). A tool may mark it as an expected failure until it does.

cases.description: A suburb starting with 'St'.

splitter.why: 'St' starts the suburb (St Marys, St Ives, St Leonards are localities). The splitter takes 'St' for a street type and splits inside the suburb, with no review flag. Under policy 1.1.x both parts are MUST, so no requirement flips, but the GT would hold a clipped locality, which skews part scoring and the role reading. Fix (README fix 1, as corrected by review finding S2): before the boundary search, match the words just before the state or postcode against the ABS localities that start with or contain a street-type word, keyed by state (52 names); a match starts the locality. Never count 'St' as a type when it is the mention's first word, right after a comma or right after a number.

cases.description: A street named in prose, other words, then a place with a comma before its state.

lines.text: She walked along Smith Street before driving to Penrith, NSW 2750.

cases.notes: No comma stands between the street and the place's suburb, so this is the no-comma split's shape; the comma after the suburb does not change the reading. Parser v4 joined the two here too.

cases.description: A numberless street with a street-type suffix ('North'), a comma and its locality, at a line start.
cases.notes: The suffix role is read on numberless streets as on numbered ones (street-suffix-comma). Parser v4 gave 'North,' the street_name role.

cases.description: A New Zealand address on one line: the town, postcode and country after the street line.

splitter.reason: no state or postcode at the end
splitter.why: An overseas address: the owner's ruling replaces it whole and keeps the country word. The splitter knows only 'Australia' as a country and only Australian states and postcodes, so it finds no state or postcode at the end and leaves the mention whole, flagged. Grading is unchanged (an unsplit ADDRESS is MUST as a whole); part scoring and the country's role are not. Fix (README fix 12): read a foreign country name at the end as the country, then the postcode in that country's shape, and never infer an Australian state from that postcode.
splitter.role_why: The end reading knows no foreign country, so it reads neither the country nor the postcode. A correct fake keeps the country words, which would then count as a leak. Same fix as the split (README fix 12).

cases.notes: The owner's ruling: an overseas address is replaced whole and the country word stays. The fake keeps the shape, with no state and no gazetteer: every number, the street name and type, the town and every postcode character change. No Australian state is inferred from the postcode. Stretch: the plan's grammar reads only Australian places (a state, an in-range postcode, 'Australia'), so no plan rule yet reads a foreign country or postcode at the end of an address. '1010' also lies in NSW's postcode range, which must not make the place a NSW one.

cases.description: Matter MX, document 5: no comma and a glued state + postcode.

splitter.reason: no state or postcode at the end
splitter.why: 'NSW2750' is a state glued to its postcode. The splitter reads neither, so it leaves the mention unsplit and flags it. Fix: read a glued state + postcode word as both.
splitter.role_why: The glued word carries the state (stays) and the postcode (changes). The end reading sees neither, so the allowance cannot cover the kept 'NSW' letters inside the fake's glued word. The evaluator needs a sub-word rule for glued words.

cases.description: Matter MX, document 8: two different addresses in one suburb get different whole fakes, each fake suburb chosen from its own address's key.
Matter MY: the same address text under another matter key gets another fake.

matters.note: One address written nine ways across eight documents: every spelling gets the same canonical fake, rendered in each original's own shape (case, abbreviation, line breaks, missing and glued parts). The street line seen alone gets the same fake street line. A different address in the same suburb gets a different whole fake.
Another matter key gives another fake for the same address text.
